business.title: A transformer-enhanced U-Net with FiLM-driven clinical conditioning for multi-task breast ultrasound lesion analysis
business.desc: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection of breast lesions using non-invasive imaging techniques is crucial for improving timely diagnosis, treatment outcomes, and patient prognosis. This study aims to develop and evaluate hybrid deep learning models for breast-lesion segmentation and classification in ultrasound images using patient-level cross-validation. Challenges such as low contrast, imaging artifacts, and irregular lesion morphology can limit accurate diagnosis, highlighting the need for advanced deep learning approaches for reliable breast-lesion analysis. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly hybrid architectures that combine convolutional and transformer representations, have shown promise in addressing these constraints. We present three Hybrid Deep Learning (HDL) models. Three complementary deep learning models were evaluated for breast lesion classification and segmentation using the Breast-Lesions-USG dataset. Model 1 employed DoubleHeadUNet with a ResNet-34 backbone, Model 2 combined a Swin V2 Transformer with a U-Net decoder, and Model 3 integrated a Hybrid Transformer-FiLM U-Net to incorporate clinical metadata. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation with strict patient separation and nested hyperparameter selection was employed. Model 1 achieved the highest accuracy (82.94%) and AUC (87.70%), while Model 3 demonstrated the highest malignant recall (81.63%) and strongest segmentation performance (Dice: 0.901; IoU: 0.825). Model 2 achieved an accuracy of 79.76% and an AUC of 87.54%. Statistical analysis indicated that most accuracy differences were not significant, supporting the complementary strengths of the three models rather than identifying a universally superior approach. Comparisons with previous studies were considered indicative due to differences in datasets and evaluation protocols.

business.title: Impact of proposed wind turbines on seismic monitoring stations at the Xiaolangdi Reservoir
business.desc: This article simulates the operation vibration of a proposed wind turbine project, analyzes its impact on existing earthquake monitoring stations in the Xiaolangdi Reservoir. It selects 2 existing wind turbines with the same power and similar surroundings as the proposed one, and uses short period seismometers, strong motion meters, and wideband seismometers to monitor vibration at different positions from the wind turbines. Based on continuous waveform recording data from each measuring point, it calculates the root mean square of vibration acceleration at short period seismometer points, ground noise acceleration at strong motion meter points, and ground noise velocity at wideband points under the start - up and shutdown states of the wind turbine. Then it compares with seismic station construction standards and evaluates if the environmental ground noise level after wind turbine operation meets regulatory requirements. The test results show that a 5.6 MW wind turbine significantly impacts within 225 m of a station with a short period digital seismometer, and impacts beyond 315 m meet relevant seismic station standards. This study provides reference for site selection, detection and analysis of new wind power generation and other vibration equipment around existing earthquake monitoring stations of the same type.

business.title: An innovative framework for student adaptability prediction using discriminant-based classification, feature selection, and sensitivity analysis
business.desc: Accurately predicting student adaptability is essential for enhancing academic performance and personal development. The present study presents a classification-based approach utilizing Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to predict student adaptability. To enhance model performance, the Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization (TFWO) and Giant Armadillo Optimization (GAO) algorithms are employed. The dataset, consisting of 1,205 student records with demographic, educational, and socio-economic attributes, is split into training and test sets. The two best-performing hybrid models undergo a sensitivity analysis using the FAST approach. Experimental results demonstrate that the QDA model optimized with GAO (QDGO) achieves the highest classification accuracy of 0.975, outperforming other model configurations. These findings underscore the potential of optimized classification models in student adaptability prediction, providing valuable insights for educational institutions. Future studies can explore additional hybrid models and larger datasets to further refine predictive accuracy.
